newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse ends session 0.37 percent lower.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse ends session 0.37 percent lower.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange closed its two hour-session on Thursday lower, pulled down mainly by some blue-chip firms, brokers said.
The all-share index closed at 478.05 points, down from 479.82 on Wednesday.
"The bourse index reacted to price drop of some blue-chip stocks...But it was just a simple adjustment of the market," a trader said.
It is the second time the index has registered a slight decline since the begining of the year. But it remained around seven percent higher, he added.

In the banking sector, blue chip Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, dropped 13 dirhams to close at 427 dirhams and Banque Marocaine pour le Commerce et l'Industrie fell seven dirhams to 352 dirhams.
Morocco's steel giant SONASID lost five dirhams to close at 355 dirhams
Ciments de l'Oriental, a leading cement firm, dropped 15 dirhams to close at 450 dirhams.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, the second largest private conglomerate, traded at 565 dirhams, up two dirhams on the previous session.
SNI, which has a market capitalisation of 5.6 billion dirhams, holds diversified stakes in more than 40 firms.
Banque Nationale pour le Developpement Economique was up four dirhams at 149 dirhams. Morocco said on Monday it would sell 34.57 percent of its stake in the bank. The tender will close on Jan 31.
Consumer credit firm Credor, floated on the bourse in December 1996 at an initial price of 385 dirhams, closed 17 dirhams higher at 582 dirhams.
The traded volume on the official market was 58.8 million dirhams from 45.4 million dirhams on the previous session. ($1= 9.1 dirhams)
